title: The Exile of El Cid
description: 1081-1094. Banished from Castile by King Alfonso VI, Rodrigo Diaz de Vivar must survive as a mercenary captain: serve the Muslim king of Zaragoza against his rivals, win battles that restore his reputation, and finally conquer Valencia in his own name. The player's small retinue grows through victories; losing El Cid himself means defeat.

anachronisms_found: SALADIN placed as the enemy hero: Salah ad-Din (1137-1193) lived a century after El Cid's exile and campaigned in Egypt/Syria, never in Iberia. The engine offers period-appropriate alternatives or a generic Castle-age enemy commander, so this was avoidable.

37 CAMEL_RIDER units as the core of the Muslim army: taifa and even Almoravid forces in eastern Iberia fought as horse cavalry (jinetes/heavy horse) and infantry; camel cavalry en masse belongs to a North African/Levantine setting, and the engine's Cavalier/Light Cavalry/Cavalry Archer would have served.
18 TREE_PALM_FOREST tiles plus ROMAN_RUINS/TEMPLE_RUIN dressing give a Near-Eastern desert look rather than the Ebro valley and Levantine huerta of Zaragoza and Valencia.

Minaya Alvar Fanez speaks throughout the dialogue but no unit represents him; conversely no representation at all of Alfonso VI, al-Mutamin of Zaragoza, Berenguer Ramon II of Barcelona, or al-Qadir/Ibn Jahhaf of Valencia, the actual named parties of 1081-1094.
